text:
The Kings got Kevin Fiala back last week, nine months after the injury he suffered at the Olympics, and that return is the best thing that has happened to them in a while. The standings have been grim: 6-11-2, 14 points, a four-game losing streak earlier this month.

Here's the uncomfortable part for anyone writing them off: our numbers say this is mostly bad luck. Los Angeles gets 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and 55% over the last ten games, which is the profile of a team that should be winning more than it loses. Instead they have 14 points against about 21 expected. The shooting has come up almost seven goals short and the goaltending has allowed almost seven too many. Darcy Kuemper, who just played his 500th game, is at .876 and four goals below expected over his last five starts.

The Adrian Kempe, Artemi Panarin and Alex Laferriere line is the engine, with 61% of the expected goals and an 8-3 goal edge. Erik Gustafsson, back after three games out per Daily Faceoff, and Brandt Clarke form the best pair. Peter Laviolette's team is 29% to make the playoffs by our odds, which is more than the record suggests. Watch Kuemper. If the saves come back, so do the points.
